questions.q: Why does this script cause an infinite loop?
options: The rule is missing a return statement
Calling current.update() inside an update-triggered rule re-triggers the same rule again, with no condition stopping it
gs.nowDateTime() is not a valid function in Business Rules
work_notes cannot be set from within a Business Rule
questions.explain: Each call to current.update() is itself an update, which re-triggers this same update rule, which calls current.update() again, and so on until the recursion limit kills the transaction.

questions.q: What's wrong with this Business Rule if it's meant to run only on insert, but is configured to also fire on update and delete?
options: It will throw a syntax error when the rule is saved
opened_at cannot be set using gs.nowDateTime()
Nothing is wrong — it behaves identically regardless of operation
It overwrites opened_at on every update too, since there's no current.operation() guard
questions.explain: Without checking current.operation() == 'insert', this logic meant for brand-new records also runs on every subsequent update, repeatedly overwriting opened_at.

questions.q: Why is this an inefficient use of the After timing?
options: After rules cannot read the current.priority field
It modifies the current record and calls current.update(), forcing a wasteful second database write that a Before rule would avoid
The rule would fail to save due to a syntax error
current.update() is not a valid method in any Business Rule
questions.explain: Since this only modifies the same record being saved, it belongs in a Before rule, where the change is folded into the one write automatically — no second current.update() call needed.

questions.q: What happens when a Business Rule has no Filter Conditions scoping when it should run?
options: It executes on every insert, update, or delete on that table, even changes unrelated to the fields it actually cares about
Filter Conditions have no effect on execution — they're purely cosmetic
The rule becomes inactive automatically
It only runs once, the first time it's activated
questions.explain: Without Filter Conditions, the rule's internal if-logic still runs on every matching database operation, wasting server resources checking changes it doesn't actually care about.

questions.q: Why is overly broad logic on a base table's Business Rule a real risk?
options: Base-table rules never actually execute due to a platform limitation
Business Rules cannot legally be created on base tables like task
A rule on task reaches every extending table, so table-specific logic without proper scoping can silently break Problem or Change Request too
It only risks affecting the Incident table and nothing else
questions.explain: Table inheritance means a rule on task fires for Incident, Problem, and Change Request alike — logic meant for only one of them needs explicit scoping or a sys_class_name guard.
